description: The pie chart illustrates a taxonomy of medical ethics, with the inner circle representing the four foundational principles of medicine: Beneficence, Justice, Non-Maleficence, and Autonomy. These four principles are depicted as large, colored segments—Beneficence in blue, Justice in orange, Non-Maleficence in purple, and Autonomy in green—each occupying a quarter of the inner circle. Radiating outward from these core principles are 26 smaller, colored segments in the outer ring, each labeled with a specific ethical category. These categories are grouped under the four main principles: Beneficence includes "Comply with Laws and Regulations," "Provide Medical Care to Patients," "Continual Learning," "Provide Assistance in Emergency," "Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues," "Respect Life, Dignity of Patients," "Give Top Priority to Patient’s Interest in Conflict of Interests," and "Minimizing Conflicts of Interest." Justice encompasses "Promote the Health of Community and Public Education," "Promote Environmental Sustainability," "Allocate Medical Sources Fairly," and "Treat Patients Fairly and Equally." Non-Maleficence includes "Prevent Patient from Harm," "Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care," and "Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct." Autonomy includes "Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain," "Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve," "Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement," "Professional Relationship with Patients and Their Relatives," "Keep Confidential," "Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication," "Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed, Freedom of Choice," and "Open Discussion and Fair Charging of Fees." The chart visually organizes the 26 detailed ethical principles into a hierarchical structure, with the outer segments arranged in a circular pattern around the central pillars, clearly showing the relationship between the broad principles and their specific applications.
